title: Stuffed shells with chicken and tomato sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed shells are large pasta shells filled with a mixture of chicken breast, cheese, and herbs, baked in a flavorful tomato sauce. The dish is a staple of Italian-inspired cuisine and is often served as a hearty lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally shells are filled with ricotta and spinach, but the chicken version has become popular in the United States.
The tomato sauce is usually made from ripe tomatoes, basil, and olive oil.
Chicken makes the filling lighter than a beef-based version.
The dish can be prepared ahead of time and reheated, making it a family favorite.
Some regions top the shells with grated Parmesan and fresh herbs before serving.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both chicken and tomato sauce contain B6 and B12, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene in tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes are high in lycopene, an antioxidant linked to reduced risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with beef‑based fillings, chicken contains less saturated fat.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese in the filling can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt; choose a low‑sodium version if you watch your sodium intake.

items.title: Food poisoning
items.content: Chicken must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate the risk of salmonella.

items.title: Gluten in pasta
items.content: Traditional shells are made from wheat and contain gluten; gluten‑free shells are needed for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, sprinkled with grated Parmesan and fresh basil. Pair with a green salad or steamed vegetables. Leftovers reheat well in the oven or microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months; reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
